what_was_done.action: Wrap missed-wave-review-dispatch.ts's act() with the dispatch-precondition gate BEFORE the run-coherence-agent fetch
what_was_done.result: Modified src/lib/reconciler-rules/missed-wave-review-dispatch.ts. Added imports for buildDispatchContext + evaluatePreconditions from ../dispatch-preconditions and appendEvent + RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED from ../event-log. Added a DISPATCH_ACTION constant pinned to 'run-coherence-agent' (what we actually fetch) AND a PRECONDITION_ACTION constant pinned to 'review-wave' (the LOGICAL action the rule is recovering — the missed dispatch was a review-wave). Added an optional repoPath?: string field to MissedWaveReviewDispatchRuleOptions (mirrors stuck-in-stage's pattern: optional for backwards-compat with the 26 existing test sites that construct the rule without repoPath; the legacy gate-skipped warn-line preserves pre-ehp.7 behaviour for those). Inside act(), AFTER the snapshot re-read and EscalationContext construction, BEFORE the AbortController/fetch sequence, when opts.repoPath is set: (a) call buildDispatchContext({ epicId, repoPath, action: PRECONDITION_ACTION='review-wave', waveNumber: snapshot.waveStatus.hasWaves ? snapshot.waveStatus.currentWave : undefined }), (b) call evaluatePreconditions(precondCtx) for the universal + per-action predicate set registered for review-wave (PLAN_FILE_MISSING, NO_WAVE_BEADS, ALL_WAVE_BEADS_CLOSED, the universal A.5 + C set). On refusal: structured warn-line tagged `reconciler_dispatch_refused` + appendEvent of type RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED to opts.repoPath with payload.ruleName='missed-wave-review-dispatch' + action='review-wave' + refusalCode + failedCheck + reason + stage='build-review' (the missed-dispatch stage); early return WITHOUT dispatching. When opts.repoPath is absent: warn-line 'precondition gate skipped — no repoPath configured' + proceed (preserves legacy test compat). Why PRECONDITION_ACTION='review-wave' rather than DISPATCH_ACTION='run-coherence-agent': the predicates we need (PLAN_FILE_MISSING for plan absence, NO_WAVE_BEADS / ALL_WAVE_BEADS_CLOSED for empty open-wave-bead set) are registered for review-wave in the EXTENDED_PRECONDITION_TABLE — they are NOT registered for run-coherence-agent because other coherence escalations target non-wave anomalies. Mirrors stuck-in-stage.ts's `precondAction = context.resumeAction` pattern at line ~430.

The placement is correct: AFTER snapshot.waveStatus.error throw (the existing pre-cutover contract preserved at lines 326-338) so we don't gate on a state we cannot determine, BEFORE the fetch.

what_was_done.action: Handle HTTP 412 from the action route as a refusal, not an HTTP failure (architecture § Seam 5 defense-in-depth)
what_was_done.result: Inserted a 412 branch ahead of the existing `if (!res.ok)` error path inside act()'s try block. If res.status === 412, read the body via res.text() (with .catch(() => '<unreadable>')), log a warn-line tagged `reconciler_dispatch_refused_at_route` with epicId/action/stage/httpStatus/body, appendEvent of type RECONCILER_ACTION_REFUSED with payload.refusalCode='ROUTE_REFUSED_412' + failedCheck='route-side-precondition' + reason=<body> + action=DISPATCH_ACTION='run-coherence-agent' (the action whose route refused), return WITHOUT throwing. Distinguishes route-side precondition refusal (race window between rule check and route check) from a genuine HTTP failure that the existing `if (!res.ok)` throw path handles. The appendEvent only fires when opts.repoPath is set (legacy compat). Mirrors marker-driven-routing.ts / wave-bead-mismatch.ts / stuck-in-stage.ts 412 handling verbatim.

surprises_or_findings:
1. PRECONDITION_ACTION vs DISPATCH_ACTION split is the load-bearing design decision. The rule actually dispatches `run-coherence-agent` (per the wlsr.15 cutover) but the precondition gate must check `review-wave` semantics — because that's the action the missed dispatch was supposed to be, and the predicates we need (PLAN_FILE_MISSING, NO_WAVE_BEADS / ALL_WAVE_BEADS_CLOSED) are registered for review-wave in EXTENDED_PRECONDITION_TABLE, NOT for run-coherence-agent. If we'd used run-coherence-agent for the gate, the wave-beads + plan-file predicates would have been skipped via appliesTo() returning false, and the gate would have been a no-op for the niii reviewer-4-wave-4-redundant case. This mirrors stuck-in-stage's `precondAction = context.resumeAction ?? 'run-coherence-agent'` pattern at line ~430 (the rule uses the action it INTENDS to recover, not the action it actually dispatches). The two constants in the rule file are pinned so the gate, fetch body, refusal logging, and 412 handling stay consistent.

2. The bead text's AC #2 'refusal with ALL_WAVE_BEADS_CLOSED' is in tension with the library's actual behaviour. Per the EXTENDED_PRECONDITION_TABLE built at dispatch-preconditions.ts line 1133+, both PRECOND_WAVE_BEADS_EXIST and PRECOND_WAVE_BEADS_NOT_ALL_CLOSED are registered for review-wave (per ehp.7's coordination requirement on the library bead — both ARE registered, verified by reading the source), and they have the same fire condition (openWaveBeadIds.length === 0) but produce different refusalCodes. PRECOND_WAVE_BEADS_EXIST is FIRST in PER_ACTION_PRECONDITIONS array order so it wins → NO_WAVE_BEADS is what fires for the niii case in practice. The bead's RISK FLAGS section names this explicitly. I followed the library's own established pattern (dispatch-preconditions.test.ts:1517 asserts refusalCode ∈ enum subset) and made the integration test enum-membership-based. This makes the test robust to a future predicate-ordering swap (if v2 introduces a real reader that disambiguates the two states, ALL_WAVE_BEADS_CLOSED could legitimately fire and the test would still pass).

3. Followed the operator-directive memory `architect-recommendations-involving-literal-grep-patterns-must-be-empirically-verified-against-the-codebase-before-bake-in`: the bead description's AC #2 phrasing 'refusal with ALL_WAVE_BEADS_CLOSED' was empirically verified against the library at dispatch-preconditions.ts lines 652-698 (PRECOND_WAVE_BEADS_EXIST and PRECOND_WAVE_BEADS_NOT_ALL_CLOSED definitions) and at lines 1133-1145 (buildExtendedTable predicate-order). Both are registered; first-to-fire-wins; v1 cannot disambiguate the two states. Bead-text literal vs library-actual reconciled in the test assertion shape per the bead's own RISK FLAGS guidance.

4. The 26 existing test sites (16 in __tests__/lib/reconciler-rules/missed-wave-review-dispatch.test.ts + 10 in __tests__/lib/missed-wave-review-dispatch.test.ts) construct the rule WITHOUT repoPath. Per the bead's SCOPE 'Out: Any change to match() logic' AND the spirit of out-of-scope updates, I made repoPath optional (mirrors stuck-in-stage's ehp.5 pattern, NOT wave-bead-mismatch's ehp.6 required-repoPath pattern). The legacy gate-skipped warn-line preserves pre-ehp.7 behaviour for those sites; bootstrap passes the production repoPath unconditionally so the production path is fully gated. All 27 existing tests pass without modification.

5. The DISPATCH_ACTION constant value matches the existing literal in the fetch body — I replaced the inline 'run-coherence-agent' string at the fetch site with the constant for symmetry with the precondition gate, refusal logging, and 412 handling. This is a small refactor (1 site) but eliminates the constant-vs-literal drift risk.
